**Keep the queued value when a restored page retries an older edit.** `wirePageHide` sends the waiting value, then clears `q.waiting` while the older request for the same field can still be in flight. If that older request then fails, `settled(true)` sees no waiting value. It writes the older value into `q.value` and calls `sendNextEdit`. The server can then finish on the older value after the newer one has arrived. This path needs the page to survive `pagehide`. A normal unload ends JavaScript execution, as the existing comment on this path states. A restore from the back/forward cache resumes the pending timeout and failure handling, so the retry can run. Whether the cache keeps a page with an outstanding request depends on the browser. When the page is restored, keep the latest value queued. A later retry then resends that value, not the older one. The `persisted` property on the `pagehide` event identifies a restore.

Review comment at @src/Application/Static/js/form-collab-runtime.js at line 1161: Update wirePageHide to use the pagehide event’s persisted property to preserve the latest queued value when the page enters the back/forward cache. Ensure that if the older request later fails and settled(true) triggers a retry, q.value still contains the newest edit rather than being replaced by the older value; preserve the existing behavior for a normal unload. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

Deferred, not patched here, per the round-2 decision on this PR (https://github.com/semitexa/semitexa-platform-ui/pull/93#issuecomment-7018821084): a page restored from the back/forward cache retrying an older edit is the same ordering problem as the two known limits, and a sequence number checked by the server (tk-collab-field-edit-server-sequence) makes a stale retry harmless in every case, this one included. The case is now listed under Known limits in the CHANGELOG (965d17f) and in that task.
